The higher-authority business evidence supports prioritizing **regulated mid-market and enterprise organizations**, not education startups. The segment analysis shows mid-market (28 accounts) and enterprise (9 accounts) together generate 83.8% of recurring revenue, with low monthly churn (2.1% and 1.3%) and strong NPS (47 and 52) [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. The Q2 performance discussion and CEO direction confirm the ICP is regulated mid-market/enterprise companies with 500–10,000 employees and high cost of incorrect answers, while SMB startups like EduVantage Labs churn at 4.8% monthly and add low expansion revenue [NL-015#NL-015-S03]. The earlier sales playbook that highlighted education startups is explicitly contradicted by these metrics, which show weaker long-term retention for smaller startups versus regulated mid-market and enterprise customers [NL-016#NL-016-S03].

The trade-off is **longer, more complex onboarding and higher acquisition cost**: mid-market onboarding averages 5.2 weeks and enterprise 8.7 weeks due to permission and security complexities, and enterprise CAC is about $22,000 versus $3,000 for SMB [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. The payoff is far higher LTV (enterprise LTV exceeding $350,000 vs. SMB capped at $25,000), lower churn, and meaningful expansion revenue ($64,000 mid-market, $91,000 enterprise in Q2) [NL-016#NL-016-S03][NL-015#NL-015-S03].
